title: Nine Pieces of Advice
subtitle: What the Prophet ﷺ told Abu ad-Darda'

content.text: Abu ad-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ advised me with nine things." (Al-Adab al-Mufrad of al-Bukhari, 18)
Do not associate anything with Allah, even if you are cut to pieces or burned.
Do not leave a prescribed prayer on purpose; whoever leaves it on purpose loses Allah's protection.
Do not drink wine, for it is the key to every evil.
Obey your parents, and if they tell you to leave your worldly goods, leave them for their sake.
Do not fight those in authority, even if you think you are in the right.
Do not run from the battlefield, even if you die and your companions flee.
Spend on your family according to your means.
Do not lift your stick from your family: never stop guiding and correcting them.
Make them mindful of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

In Arabic: عَنْ أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ قَالَ: أَوْصَانِي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِتِسْعٍ: لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ قُطِّعْتَ أَوْ حُرِّقْتَ، وَلَا تَتْرُكَنَّ الصَّلَاةَ الْمَكْتُوبَةَ مُتَعَمِّدًا، وَمَنْ تَرَكَهَا مُتَعَمِّدًا بَرِئَتْ مِنْهُ الذِّمَّةُ، وَلَا تَشْرَبَنَّ الْخَمْرَ فَإِنَّهَا مِفْتَاحُ كُلِّ شَرٍّ، وَأَطِعْ وَالِدَيْكَ وَإِنْ أَمَرَاكَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ مِنْ دُنْيَاكَ فَاخْرُجْ لَهُمَا، وَلَا تُنَازِعَنَّ وُلَاةَ الْأَمْرِ وَإِنْ رَأَيْتَ أَنَّكَ أَنْتَ، وَلَا تَفْرُرْ مِنَ الزَّحْفِ وَإِنْ هَلَكْتَ وَفَرَّ أَصْحَابُكَ، وَأَنْفِقْ مِنْ طَوْلِكَ عَلَى أَهْلِكَ، وَلَا تَرْفَعْ عَصَاكَ عَنْ أَهْلِكَ، وَأَخِفْهُمْ فِي اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ

The words are وَلَا تَرْفَعْ عَصَاكَ عَنْ أَهْلِكَ, literally "do not lift your stick away from your family". The scholars explain it as a figure of speech: do not neglect their upbringing and discipline. It is not a command to hit. The Prophet ﷺ himself never struck a woman or a servant, as 'A'ishah reported (Muslim).
